# Design Handoff: YouTube Embed Protection
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent) on behalf of Agno JF

## Outcome

Keep YouTube as the MVP video host while reducing casual video-link discovery, preserving a one-step administrator workflow, and recording the unavoidable browser-level URL-sharing limitation.

## Approved Workflow

| User | Workflow |
|---|---|
| Administrator | Paste a YouTube watch URL, short URL, embed URL, or complete iframe embed code into the existing video field and submit the session form. |
| Application | Extract and validate the YouTube video ID, store a canonical watch URL, and generate the controlled embed configuration. |
| Participant | Open a published session through an authenticated active account and play the embedded recording inside the application. |
| Guest or revoked user | Fail the existing server-side route and active-user checks before receiving the session or video embed. |

## Protection Target

- Protect the application session page and the application-managed participant boundary.
- Keep unpublished sessions unavailable to participants.
- Reduce visible YouTube navigation and sharing controls in the normal player experience.
- Avoid exposing raw administrator input or arbitrary pasted HTML to participant pages.
- Do not claim that the YouTube video ID is secret after an authorized participant receives the player.

## Acceptance Boundary

The build may pass its local implementation checks when:

- The administrator can save each supported input form with one paste and one submit.
- Invalid or non-YouTube input is rejected with a field error.
- The stored value is a canonical YouTube watch URL, not pasted iframe HTML.
- Participant responses contain the generated privacy-enhanced embed URL only after server-side authorization.
- The generated player requests reduced native controls and the application provides accessible playback controls.
- Existing guest, unpublished-session, and revoked-user protections remain intact.
- Tests document that an authenticated browser can still recover the YouTube video ID.

RQ-17 remains a residual-risk decision. This build does not close `ACT-02 (Test embedded-video configuration against URL copying or discovery and define acceptable protection for the Option B application)` or `R-12 (Authenticated members may copy or discover the URL of an embedded video)`.

## PM Decision Recorded

The PM accepted the residual outcome on 2026-08-20 under `D-15 (Accept the standard YouTube embed limitation for MVP session recordings)`. YouTube is acceptable for MVP recordings when the application controls page access and reduces casual discovery, but it cannot prevent an authenticated participant from inspecting or sharing the YouTube URL. LeadLab Director final launch acceptance remains separate.
